source.stem:
Which is the value of a vector quantity?
A 200 V
B 3
100 kg / m
C 20 m / s, east
D 50 J / (kg ° C)

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: spring balance is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Use the actual range and divisions of the spring balance being read.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: least count of the spring balance -> smallest weight value that can be read happens first, and that produces scale interval and number of small divisions.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Use the actual range and divisions of the spring balance being read is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: For a spring balance, the smallest readable value is found by dividing the weight difference between two bigger marks by the number of small divisions between them; in the shown example, 1 N divided by 5 gives 0.2 N. scale interval and number of small divisions -> least count of the spring balance -> smallest weight value that can be read The learner correctly applies this rule: For a spring balance, the smallest readable value is found by dividing the weight difference between two bigger marks by the number of small divisions between them; in the shown example, 1 N divided by 5 gives 0.2 N. The smallest readable value is whichever number on the spring balance looks largest or most prominent.
